description: How the supporter coin is framed and turned, once per shell. The MODEL is shared (assets/coin/futo-coin.glb / .usdz) and so is the studio that lights it, but each renderer is handed the numbers separately: resting spin 1.25 rad/s, spin decay 2.6, 0.018 radians per pixel/dp/point of drag, flick clamped to 0.6..24 rad/s, tilt 0.24 rad, a 30 degree vertical field of view at distance 1.55, and a frame-delta clamp of 1/20 s. Since 2026-09-18 also the TAP QUEUE: one full turn owed per tap, paid back at 3 rad/s per radian owed, clamped to 2..26 rad/s, settled below 0.01 rad, and a tap recognised as a press that moved 5px/dp/pt or less and lasted 400ms or less. Also the orientation LAW: tilt about X first, then spin about Y, so the coin turns on a fixed tilted spindle rather than wobbling.
note: Partial: the orientation law is locked on Android by SupporterCoinTest (`the spindle does not move as the coin turns`) and on iOS by SupporterCoinTests, which is the one way to get this wrong that still looks plausible on a still screenshot -- composing tilt and spin in the other order swings the spindle and the coin wobbles like a dropped hubcap. TypeScript writes the same law as pivot.rotation.x/y, untested, so it can still drift from the two native shells. The TAP QUEUE is locked on all three: `supporterCoin.test.ts`, `SupporterCoinTest` and `SupporterCoinTests` each run the debt frame by frame and insist ten taps deliver ten turns; all three were red-proved against the restart-per-tap model they replaced. The motion constants themselves are unlocked everywhere: nothing but you keeps the three in step, so touch all three in one commit and say so. Note that the per-shell LIGHT LEVEL is deliberately NOT shared -- Filament measures indirect light in different units than three.js and RealityKit -- but all three are calibrated against the SAME reference, the desktop renderer at exposure 1.0 (@justin 2026-09-18: 'desktop is just right'). Desktop TONE_MAPPING_EXPOSURE 1.0, Android IBL_INTENSITY 1.25, iOS coinLightExponent -0.75. The previous Android 4.5 came from a false premise -- its comment claimed cmgen normalises the cubemap, and it does not: studio-env-ibl.ktx carries absolute radiance (mean 3.41 vs the .hdr's 3.15, peak 47.0 vs 46.75). Re-measure all three together, never one alone; the method is in each constant's comment and the desktop half is `just coin-tuner`.
